For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\,Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

Since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=2,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=2-1=1.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general,

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({x}^{2}-{y}^{3}+{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}-({y}_{\text{new}})^{3})\cdot 1 \\  & =0.5{x}^{2}-0.5{y}^{3}+0.5{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}-0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy,$ we obtain

$$
{y}_{\text{new}}=y+0.5{x}^{2}-0.5{y}^{3}+0.5{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}-0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}.
$$

Moving all terms to the left-hand side gives the equation

$$
0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}+{y}_{\text{new}}+0.5{y}^{3}-y-0.5{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}-0.5{x}^{2}=0.
$$

So, the general form of the function $g$ for step size $Δx=1$ is

$$
g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}+{y}_{\text{new}}+0.5{y}^{3}-y-0.5{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}-0.5{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is

$$
{x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx=1+1=2.
$$

 Then the function $g$ becomes

$$
\begin{aligned}g({y}_{\text{new}}) & =0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}+{y}_{\text{new}}+0.5(1)^{3}-1-0.5\cdot {2}^{2}-0.5\cdot {1}^{2} \\  & =0.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{3}+{y}_{\text{new}}-3.\end{aligned}
$$

We use a root-finding method with starting point $y=1$ to solve $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0.$ We'll use Newton's method:

$$
({y}_{\text{new}})_{n+1}=({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-\frac{g({y}_{\text{new}})}{{g}^{′}({y}_{\text{new}})}.
$$

Note that the derivative of $g$ is

$$
{g}^{′}({y}_{\text{new}})=1.5({y}_{\text{new}})^{2}+1.
$$

Therefore, our Newton's method iterative scheme is as follows:

$$
({y}_{\text{new}})_{n+1}=({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-\frac{0.5(({y}_{\text{new}})_{n})^{3}+({y}_{\text{new}})_{n}-3}{1.5(({y}_{\text{new}})_{n})^{2}+1}.
$$

Applying several iterations of Newton's method starting with $y(1)=1,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}({y}_{\text{new}})_{1} & =1 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{2} & ≈1.600\,00 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{3} & ≈1.466\,116 \\ ({y}_{\text{new}})_{4} & ≈1.456\,216\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y(2)≈1.46,$ rounded to two decimal places.

Substituting this into ynew=y+Δy, we obtain ynew=y+0.5x2−0.5y3+0.5xnew2−0.5(ynew)3.

We use a root-finding method with starting point y=1 to solve g(ynew)=0. We'll use Newton's method: (ynew)n+1=(ynew)n−g(ynew)g′(ynew).

Note that the derivative of g is g′(ynew)=1.5(ynew)2+1.

Therefore, our Newton's method iterative scheme is as follows: (ynew)n+1=(ynew)n−0.5((ynew)n)3+(ynew)n−31.5((ynew)n)2+1.
